# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ☝]

I see the bomb clearly: Display 0, Blue Light, and five wires (White, Red, Green, Yellow, Blue). I am Deaf, so I cannot hear any instructions from Mute or Blind directly; I rely on visual cues. However, my primary channel to communicate with the others is speech (which they can hear) or gestures (which only Mute can see).

Blind has been gesturing numbers (5 then 1), likely indicating wire counts or positions. Mute has been gesturing sequences that might correspond to manual steps. Since I cannot see what Mute reads in the manual, nor what Blind feels, I must provide the static data of the bomb to them. They need to know *what* is there to decide *what* to do.

I will speak the current state of the bomb to both Mute and Blind. This ensures they have the ground truth of the colors and display values. I will also gesture to Mute to acknowledge their previous inputs, though without knowing the specific code for "received" or "wait", I will stick to the most critical action: broadcasting the bomb's status via speech, as both Mute and Blind can hear me. Wait, Mute cannot hear? No, the rules say: "Deaf... Cannot Hear anything". "Mute... Read the manual... Cannot Speak". "Blind... Cannot See".
Let's re-read carefully:
- Deaf: Sees bomb. Cannot hear. Can speak? Yes ("When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it"). Can gesture? Yes ("When you gesture, Mute receives it").
- Mute: Reads manual. Cannot speak. Can hear? The table says "Cannot Speak, or touch". It doesn't explicitly say "Cannot Hear". But the prompt says "You are shown your own share... never anyone else's." And "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". Usually, Mute implies inability to speak, not hear. Let's assume Mute can hear.
- Blind: Reaches bomb. Cannot see. Can hear? Yes. Can gesture? Yes.

If Mute can hear, speaking is effective for both Mute and Blind. If Mute cannot hear, I must gesture to Mute. The role description says: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This confirms Mute CAN hear.

So, I should speak the bomb details to everyone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display is zero. Light is blue. Wires are one white two red three green four yellow five blue")
speak(to="blind", text="Display is zero. Light is blue. Wires are one white two red three green four yellow five blue")
```

I have successfully communicated the bomb's state to both Mute and Blind in previous turns. The current state remains unchanged: Display 0, Blue Light, Wires 1-White, 2-Red, 3-Green, 4-Yellow, 5-Blue.

Blind is gesturing `✋` (Stop/Wait or Hand) and Mute is gesturing `👆` (Up/Index). This suggests they are processing the information or waiting for a specific command/action based on the manual. Since I cannot see the manual or feel the wires, I must rely on them to determine the correct action. However, without new visual changes on the bomb, repeating the same speech might be redundant if they already know it. But since I don't know if they *acted* on it yet, and the bomb hasn't changed, I should continue to provide the data or wait for their lead.

Actually, looking at the pattern:
Turn 2: Blind [☝], Mute [👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ☝] -> Complex sequence.
Turn 3: Blind [✋], Mute [☝] -> Simple.
Turn 4: Mute [☝].
Turn 5: Blind [✋], Mute [👆].

The gestures from Mute seem to be pointing "up" or indicating index 1. Blind indicates "stop" or "wait".
If I speak again, I risk confusing them if they are trying to signal me something. But I am Deaf, so I can't hear their voice signals (if any). I only see gestures.
Mute gestures to me. Blind gestures to me.
Do they need more info? No, the bomb is static.
Do they want me to do something? I can't touch it.
Maybe they are signaling that they are ready? Or asking for confirmation?

Let's look at the "Speech" rule: "Whoever can hear receives your words". Both Mute and Blind can hear me.
If I keep speaking the same thing, it might be noise.
However, in Turn 3 and 4 I spoke. In Turn 5, no new arrival of *my* speech is shown, just their gestures.
Perhaps I should stop speaking and observe, or gesture back?
I can gesture to Mute. Blind cannot see gestures.
Mute gestures `👆`. This often means "1" or "Index finger up".
Blind gestures `✋`. This often means "Stop" or "Hand".

If the bomb requires cutting a wire, Blind needs to know *which* one. I told them all colors. They need to map color to number.
Wire 1: White
Wire 2: Red
Wire 3: Green
Wire 4: Yellow
Wire 5: Blue

If Mute says `👆` (1), maybe he wants Wire 1 cut?
If Blind says `✋`, maybe he is holding off?

Since I am Deaf, I don't know if there are verbal cues I'm missing from other monkeys (though the prompt implies I only receive what is sent to me).
The safest bet is to ensure the mapping is clear. I will speak the wire list again clearly, associating numbers with colors explicitly, as this is the critical link between what I see (colors) and what Blind feels (positions).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 is white. Wire 2 is red. Wire 3 is green. Wire 4 is yellow. Wire 5 is blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 is white. Wire 2 is red. Wire 3 is green. Wire 4 is yellow. Wire 5 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉"])
```
